clue.text: Leader of caliphate slyly hoards head coverings worn by women in Iraq

definitions.text: head coverings worn by women in Iraq

indicators.note: the leader of a group is the one at the front, so only the opening letter of the next word is kept
acting slyly means moving deviously, so the word it qualifies is rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of caliphate
the six letters of hoards, rearranged

explanation.surface: A caliph's leader is pictured stockpiling the veils that Iraqi women wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A chador is the full-length cloak and veil worn by many Muslim women, so the plural answers the long descriptive definition.

clue.text: Gangster stops before the end, being chicken

indicators.note: stopping short of the end means the final letter never arrives

blocks.note: Al Capone, the Chicago mobster

explanation.surface: A mobster quits before the finish, showing himself a coward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' suggests cowardice, which suits the gangster quitting; it is the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated rooster fattened for the table, a type of chicken.

clue.text: Unearthly carnage or hubris

indicators.note: something unearthly is weird and unnatural, so these letters take a strange new form

blocks.note: all nine letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A choice between supernatural slaughter and overweening pride.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unearthly' wants to be the definition; it is the anagram signal, and hubris is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubris is excessive pride, the Greek-tragedy flaw, and arrogance is its everyday synonym.

clue.text: Eject our team in overtime

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: OT is the abbreviation for overtime
our team is us

explanation.surface: A fan complains that the referee threw their team out in extra time.
explanation.definitionFit: To oust someone is to drive them out of a place or position, the same as throwing them out.

clue.text: Total Dean's car

indicators.note: to total a vehicle is to wreck it, so the letters are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: the five letters of Dean's

explanation.surface: Someone has written off Dean's automobile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Total' is American slang for wrecking a car beyond repair, which fits the surface perfectly.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan is the American name for a saloon, an enclosed four-door passenger car.

clue.text: Communist figure, at present, is a prisoner

blocks.note: Ho Chi Minh, the Vietnamese Communist leader
to present a play is to stage it

explanation.surface: It reads like a news line about a Communist leader who is currently behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At present' looks like one phrase meaning 'now'; split it, and 'at' just places the leader beside the verb present.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostage is a person held captive as security for a demand, so a kind of prisoner.

clue.text: One who encourages second choice for pork as a fast-food standard?

blocks.note: ham is cured pork
B is plan B, the second option
one who urges others on

explanation.surface: Someone backing a substitute for pork as a fast-food menu staple.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are read in reverse clue order. 'For' just places the second choice beside the pork; nothing is substituted.
explanation.definitionFit: The burger is the staple item of fast-food chains, and the question mark flags the beef patty's name containing ham.

clue.text: In the morning, soldiers resurrected a character from Sophocles

indicators.note: something resurrected rises up, and in a down answer rising means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: AM is ante meridiem, the morning
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: Dawn sees soldiers bringing a figure from Greek tragedy back to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character' suggests a person in a play; here it is a letter of the Greek alphabet Sophocles wrote in.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the Greek letter S, so it is a written character a Greek author like Sophocles used.

clue.text: Counters a taxi climbing on the far side of Fiji

indicators.note: climbing goes upward, and in a down answer that means the taxi word reads from the bottom
the far side of a word is its last letter

blocks.note: taken as written
a cab is a taxi
the last letter of Fiji

explanation.surface: Hailing a cab heading uphill on the remote side of a Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: Fiji is also one of the three theme countries named in the clues rather than hidden in answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Abaci is the plural of abacus, the bead frame used for counting, so these are counting devices.

clue.text: In fact, decapitated seabird is inside for all time

indicators.note: losing a head means losing the first letter
being inside means sitting within the other word

blocks.note: really, as in actually, in fact
a tern is a slender seabird

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: a beheaded seabird lies within, to stay there forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Decapitated' seems to go with seabird, but it beheads the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternally means without end, forever, which is what lasting for all time is.

clue.text: Looked over pedestrian, concealing stratagem

indicators.note: something concealing another thing holds it out of sight inside itself

blocks.note: PED is the standard short form of pedestrian, as on American road signs
a ruse is a crafty stratagem

explanation.surface: Someone eyes a passer-by who is hiding a cunning plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pedestrian' tempts as the adjective meaning dull; it is the walker, shortened as on street signs.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to read or examine something, so the past tense matches a past-tense phrase for inspecting.

clue.text: Tycoon is a pest in West

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside it

blocks.note: Mae West, the American film star
a gnat is a small biting insect, a pest

explanation.surface: A business baron is branded a nuisance out in the western states.
explanation.walkthrough: West looks like a region, but it is Mae West, whose first name wraps the insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A magnate is a wealthy, powerful business figure, a synonym for an industrial tycoon.

clue.text: Nearly stable sound without error

indicators.note: going without something means leaving it out, so one letter is dropped

blocks.note: the noise a horse makes in its stable
E is the scorebook abbreviation for an error in baseball

explanation.surface: It reads as a description of something almost steady and close to flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nearly stable' looks like one phrase; 'Nearly' is the definition and 'stable sound' is the horse's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Nigh is an old-fashioned adverb for almost, as in 'nigh on impossible'.

clue.text: Weird bionic tuna is preparing to hatch

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the definition reads as a verb phrase, the state of an egg being incubated

indicators.note: weird means strange or out of the usual, so these letters come out in an odd new order

blocks.note: all ten letters of the two words

explanation.surface: A strange cyborg fish is about to come out of its egg.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubation is the period of keeping eggs warm until they hatch, so it describes an egg getting ready to hatch.

clue.text: Where Laos is allowing some investment activity, initially

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so each word gives its first letter

blocks.note: the first letters of the four words

explanation.surface: A note on how Laos is beginning to open up to foreign investment.
explanation.walkthrough: Laos is one of the three theme countries named in the clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Laos is a landlocked country in Southeast Asia, so the continent is its location.

clue.text: Gets sharp to follow Mel on the baseball field in comeback — no fooling

indicators.note: a comeback returns the way it came, so these words are read backwards

blocks.note: to hone a blade is to sharpen it
to dog someone is to follow them
Mel Ott, the New York Giants slugger

explanation.surface: A baseball tale of a player making a comeback after Mel Ott, sworn to be true.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To follow' reads as a link but is the verb dog; Mel Ott was a Hall of Fame outfielder.
explanation.definitionFit: Honest to God is an emphatic oath of sincerity, the same assurance as saying you are not joking.

clue.text: Thin proof after a stampede!

indicators.note: after a stampede everything is trampled into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: all nine letters of the two words

explanation.surface: There is hardly any evidence left once a herd has stampeded through.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: a single track is slim evidence left behind by a stampede.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoofprint is the mark left in the ground by a hoof, the trace a stampeding herd leaves.

clue.text: Extremely sensitive experiment about finalist?

indicators.note: about means going around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: a test is a trial or experiment
one who comes at the finish, playfully coined; the question mark admits it

explanation.surface: A study probing how delicate a contestant in the final feels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' looks like an outer-letters signal; it builds the superlative of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tenderest is the superlative of tender, meaning sore or easily hurt, so most sensitive.

clue.text: Cross-dressing ultimately enlivened tabloid

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so only the closing letter of the word after it is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of enlivened
a rag is a cheap, sensational newspaper

explanation.surface: A gossip paper perked up by a cross-dressing scandal.
explanation.definitionFit: Drag is clothing of the opposite sex worn for performance, as in drag queens.

clue.text: Miss rock a lot

blocks.note: a miss is a young woman, a gal
ore is rock that metal is mined from

explanation.surface: A young woman sways back and forth a great deal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock a lot' looks like a verb phrase about swaying; rock is the mineral and 'a lot' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Galore means in abundance, placed after its noun as in 'prizes galore', so it means plenty.

clue.text: Gland is so diseased, it is sliding

indicators.note: something diseased is in a bad state, so these letters are disordered

blocks.note: all nine letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A medical note: the gland is infected and slipping out of place.
explanation.definitionFit: Glissando is a musical direction from Italian-French glisser, to glide, for sliding rapidly up or down a scale.

clue.text: See 17
Something unusual Blair may not set right

indicators.note: setting things right means rearranging them into proper order

blocks.note: all eleven letters of the three words

explanation.surface: A political jab: there is a strange problem that Tony Blair may fail to fix.
explanation.walkthrough: Tony Blair was the British prime minister from 1997 to 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: An abnormality is a feature or event that departs from the norm, an irregular thing.

clue.text: Playwright and detective managed computer company with love

blocks.note: PI is a private investigator
to run a business is to manage it
Dell, the American PC maker
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A list of jobs: a dramatist and a sleuth ran a tech firm, with affection.
explanation.definitionFit: Luigi Pirandello was the Italian dramatist of Six Characters in Search of an Author.

clue.text: Listening to tenant's gossip

indicators.note: listening means we judge the word by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a roomer is one who rents a room, a tenant

explanation.surface: Eavesdropping on the latest chatter of the lodger downstairs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking the wordplay to the definition. RUMOR is the American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: A rumor is an unverified story passed from person to person, which is what gossip is.

clue.text: Medical professional heard running through inner city

indicators.note: something heard running through a spoken phrase is a sound carried in the middle of it, judged by ear rather than spelling

blocks.note: spoken aloud, the middle of the phrase carries the sound of the answer

explanation.surface: A doctor's familiar voice is heard hurrying through a run-down downtown district.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters do not spell the answer in the phrase; only its sound does, as 'inner city' is said in-ner-ci-ty.
explanation.definitionFit: A nurse is a trained health-care worker who cares for patients, a medical professional.

clue.text: Body of knowledge covering Northern actress

indicators.note: a cover goes over and around what it covers

blocks.note: lore is traditional knowledge
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A reference book on a film star from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The N sits at the end of LORE, which is the covering word's final place.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophia Loren is the Italian film actress, an Oscar winner for Two Women.

clue.text: A blackjack stat

blocks.note: taken as written
a sap is a short leather cosh, also called a blackjack

explanation.surface: It reads like a card player's figure from the blackjack table.
explanation.walkthrough: Blackjack suggests the card game; here it is the club. Stat is hospital jargon from Latin statim.
explanation.definitionFit: Stat is the doctors' word for immediately, and ASAP abbreviates as soon as possible.

clue.text: A couple of bards!

blocks.note: Edgar Allan Poe, the American poet
T. S. Eliot, the modernist poet, by his initials

explanation.surface: An exclamation pointing at two poets.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue does both jobs: two poets join to spell the word for poets in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Bards are poets, so the plural answer describes a pair of them, and the two named poets make it.

clue.text: Skip address to Cambridge University?

blocks.note: O is the vocative address, as in 'O Romeo'
the Massachusetts Institute of Technology is in Cambridge, Massachusetts; the question mark warns it is not Cambridge, England

explanation.surface: Should a student bother with a speech to Cambridge University?
explanation.walkthrough: Cambridge University suggests the English one; it is the American institute in Cambridge, Massachusetts.
explanation.definitionFit: To omit something is to leave it out, which is what skipping it means.

clue.text: Root at first for McCain's ending in enormous plunge

indicators.note: what comes at first is the opening letter of the word before it
a word's ending is its final letter
one thing for another means it stands in its place

blocks.note: the first letter of Root
the last letter of McCain
immense means enormous

explanation.surface: An election story: rooting for John McCain as his support takes a huge fall.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter of Root takes the place of the letter of McCain inside the word for enormous.
explanation.definitionFit: To immerse something is to dip or submerge it completely, which is what plunging does.

clue.text: Spilled cream on novel

indicators.note: something spilled lands in a mess, so these letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: all seven letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone has knocked cream over a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like the adjective meaning new; it is the book.
explanation.definitionFit: A romance is a love story, a genre of book, so a type of novel.

clue.text: Make life difficult for dudes caught in unlawful act

indicators.note: being caught in something means being trapped inside it

blocks.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
dudes are guys, men

explanation.surface: Police harass some guys found committing a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment someone is to cause them suffering or keep pestering them, which makes their life hard.

clue.text: Unfortunately, no — it's an array of four-letter names hidden in seven of the Across entries (the other three are in the clues)

definitions.text: array of four-letter names hidden in seven of the Across entries (the other three are in the clues)

indicators.note: things going unfortunately go wrong, so these letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: the letters of no, it's and an

explanation.surface: A regretful 'no', then an explanation of the puzzle's hidden theme.
explanation.walkthrough: The ten four-letter countries: CHAD, PERU, CUBA, TOGO, MALI, IRAN and OMAN hide in Across answers; IRAQ, FIJI and LAOS appear in the clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Each hidden name is a country, and countries are nations, so the theme set is a group of nations.
